title: Acyclic Hom from bounded-above acyclic sums of Ext-orthogonal modules
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site in the chosen universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $F$ an $R$-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $(E_i)_{i\in I}$ be a set-indexed family of $R$-module sheaves such that $\operatorname{Ext}_R^p(E_i,F)=0$ for every $i\in I$ and $p>0$, where $\operatorname{Ext}_R^p(E_i,F)=H^p\operatorname{Hom}_R(E_i,J^\bullet)$ for an injective resolution $F\to J^\bullet$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Let $K^\bullet$ be a bounded above acyclic cochain complex of $R$-module sheaves [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules], and suppose every $K^n$ is isomorphic to a small coproduct of members of this family, with repetitions allowed. Then the cochain complex of abelian groups $\operatorname{Hom}_R(K^\bullet,F)$ is acyclic. Its term in degree $n$ is $\operatorname{Hom}_R(K^{-n},F)$ and its differential sends $h$ to $(-1)^{n+1}h\circ d_K^{-n-1}$.

source.place: Tag 07AA, example-hom-complex-into-sheaf, second spectral sequence, with the coproduct/Ext-orthogonality application written in the proof of lemma-existence-derived-lower-shriek.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-coproduct-ext-resolution-cohomology] to the given site, $R$, $F$ and family. Fix the nonnegative augmented injective resolution $F\to J^\bullet$ it supplies. Its resolution-independence assertion puts the Ext hypothesis on this fixed resolution. For each term of $K$, the same lemma and the specified coproduct isomorphism give $H^q\operatorname{Hom}_R(K^r,J^\bullet)=0$ for $q>0$ and the natural degree-zero identification with $\operatorname{Hom}_R(K^r,F)$.

source.place: Tags 07AA (example-hom-complex-into-sheaf, choice of injective resolution and column cohomology) and 07AC (lemma-existence-derived-lower-shriek, passage from positive Ext vanishing on summands to their direct sums). Expanded coproduct/product and degree-zero comparison from the parent proof, old steps 1, 2 and 4.

proof.text: Choose $b\in\mathbf Z$ with $K^r=0$ for $r>b$. The resolution from step 1 has $J^q=0$ for $q<0$ and injective terms; $K$ is acyclic by hypothesis. Thus apply [lem-trf-acyclic-injective-hom-bicomplex] to $K,b,J$. It constructs $D^{p,q}=\operatorname{Hom}_R(K^{b-p},J^q)$ with horizontal precomposition and vertical postcomposition. Its statement gives exactness of every row, including $p=0$, and acyclicity of $\operatorname{Tot}D$ in every degree.

source.place: Tag 07AA, example-hom-complex-into-sheaf, the Hom double complex and its other filtration, used in Tag 07AC, lemma-existence-derived-lower-shriek, zero abutment for an acyclic source. Explicit first-quadrant reindexing, injective extension at every row including its endpoint, and finite-filtration argument from the parent proof, old steps 3, 5 and 6.

proof.text: By step 2, $D$ is a first-quadrant double complex in $\operatorname{Ab}$ with finite total diagonals. The first spectral sequence of [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences] has ${}'E_1^{p,q}=H^q\operatorname{Hom}_R(K^{b-p},J^\bullet)$. By [lem-trf-coproduct-ext-resolution-cohomology] and step 1, only $q=0$ remains, naturally identified with $C^p=\operatorname{Hom}_R(K^{b-p},F)$, $d_C(h)=h\circ d_K^{b-p-1}$ for $p\geq0$. Naturality makes $d_1=d_C$. Hence ${}'E_2^{p,0}=H^p(C)$ and all other rows vanish. The finite-filtration convergence supplied by the spectral-sequence theorem satisfies [lem-weil-pbc-first-quadrant-row-collapse]. Its edge isomorphism in every $p\geq0$, including zero, gives $H^p(C)\cong H^p(\operatorname{Tot}D)=0$ by step 2.

source.place: Tag 07AC, lemma-existence-derived-lower-shriek, final spectral-sequence paragraph; Tag 07AA, example-hom-complex-into-sheaf; homology.tex Tag 0132, lemma-first-quadrant-ss.

proof.text: Finally put $T^n=\operatorname{Hom}_R(K^{-n},F)$ with the differential in the statement. Degree relabelling gives $T^{p-b}=C^p$ for $p\ge0$ and $T^n=0$ for $n<-b$. On this relabelled complex the differential is $(-1)^{p-b+1}d_C$. Choose signs $a_0=1$ and $a_{p+1}=(-1)^{p-b+1}a_p$. Multiplication by $a_p$ gives an isomorphism from $C^p$ to $T^{p-b}$, since $a_{p+1}d_C=(-1)^{p-b+1}d_Ca_p$; its inverse is multiplication by the same signs. It therefore identifies $H^p(C)$ with $H^{p-b}(T)$. These groups vanish by step 3, and all lower degrees of $T$ are zero. This proves acyclicity with precisely the specified Hom differential.

source.place: Tag 07AC, lemma-existence-derived-lower-shriek, concluding acyclicity of the Hom complex; explicit sign comparison with the convention in the item.
